new_write_endpoint_input_validation.notes: POST /api/secrets/vault-name-override validates every field via express-validator before any GitHub call: vaultDir (1-512 chars), name (1-256), resourceGroup (optional, 1-256), appName (^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$), environment (^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,32}$), target (enum 'live'|'sand'), qualifier (optional, ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$) — identical regex conventions to the existing GET /api/secrets/:appName/:environment route. A 400 short-circuits before any resolveKeyVaults() or GitHub call. Beyond schema validation, the endpoint also enforces a server-side allow-list check (calls resolveKeyVaults()/matchVaultsFromEntries and rejects with 422 if the submitted vaultDir is not among the vaults actually discovered for appName/environment/target/qualifier) before writing — prevents a client from writing an override for an arbitrary/non-existent vaultDir path (path-traversal-adjacent risk), matching the existing submitSecretViaGitOps() allow-list pattern.

optimistic_concurrency_sha_handling.notes: setVaultNameOverride() reads the sidecar via githubService.getFileContent() (returns { content, sha } or null on 404), merges the entry, and calls createOrUpdateFile(repo, branch, path, content, message, file ? file.sha : null). githubService.createOrUpdateFile() passes sha through to Octokit's createOrUpdateFileContents; a stale sha causes GitHub to reject with an HTTP 409/422/412-class error, which githubService re-throws with .status intact (confirmed by reading services/githubService.js lines 267-295 — no swallowing). setVaultNameOverride() catches exactly error.status in {409,422,412} and rethrows as err.code='CONFLICT', which routes/api.js maps to HTTP 409 with correlationId. No data-loss path: a concurrent edit is never overwritten blindly, the client must re-read and retry. Verified against tests/integration/service/vaultNameOverrideRoute.spec.ts's 409-mapping test.

no_secret_or_pii_leakage_in_new_log_line.notes: Reviewed every new log/logMetric call in secretsService.js and routes/api.js for this feature: fields logged are vaultDir, source, appName, environment, target, qualifier, error.message, and req.user?.email (verifiedBy/user) — all consistent with existing repo-wide logging conventions (user email is already logged on every other /api/secrets/* and /api/apps route, not a new PII exposure class). No Key Vault secret value, override content beyond name/resourceGroup (which are Key Vault names/RG identifiers, not secret material), or GitHub token/credential ever appears in a log line. grep across services/secretsService.js confirms secretValue-handling code (encryptValueWithSops, 0600 temp file) is pre-existing and untouched by this feature.
